findings.defect: Cumulus seen from the pad read as sculpted putty at a glance. (1) Bodies are smooth, with no cauliflower detail at any scale; edges are a 2-4 px soft ramp, so the clouds look out of focus against the sharp terrain. (2) Undersides are fluted: long smeared streaks that all point along the view rays (clouds-ground-cumulus.png x 60-540, y 120-380), like pulled taffy. (3) No flat dark bases and no bright sunlit tops: underside and flank are the same light grey. (4) With a uniform map at coverage 0.4, under 1 % of the frame above the horizon is blue sky (pixels with B - R > 28): the field is nearly closed and the 'gaps' are milky grey (x 900-1100, y 80-260). (5) perf-pad-1440p.png has a translucent fan with a defined curved rim hanging in clear sky (x 800-1100, y 380-760 at 1440p). (6) One march-step in from the edge the cloud is a featureless grey gradient (clouds-ascent-2kms-1800m-*.png).
findings.realReference: Fair-weather cumulus at noon: crisp white cauliflower turrets with detail down to a few metres, hard sunlit edges against saturated blue, flat bases two to three stops darker than the tops, clear blue between individual clouds at 40 % cover, bases receding to the horizon in perspective rows.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/atmosphere/shaders/clouds.ts. Noise is read one mip above the footprint (lodB = log2(footprint * noiseBase.w * 256); the 128^3 base tile over 9,000 m is 70 m per texel, so nothing under about 150-300 m survives), and 'footprint = max(pixel, 0.25 * ruleDt)' ties the mip to the step length (stepMaxM 600), which blurs along the ray and produces the radial flutes. Detail erosion is a 32^3 texture displacing the surface by at most detailErosion 0.24 and is gone by detailFadeFootprintM 400. The threshold is lowered by 0.5 k (thr = 1 - cLow - 0.5 k) plus fairWeatherCoverage and the mesoscale term, which over-covers. Lighting: the two-stream 'highOrders' term and the ground/sky ambient make the base as bright as the flank. Half-resolution buffer, one ray per 2 x 2 block, plain bilinear upsample in the march (textureSampleLevel(cloudTex, linearClamp, uvCloud)).
findings.fixDirection: Decouple the noise mip from the step length (use the pixel footprint only; handle long steps by more steps inside resolved cloud, not by blurring). Add real high-frequency structure: a 64^3 or larger detail texture with curl distortion, eroding by remapping density (Schneider/Hillaire style), and keep it to the pixel footprint. Derive coverage so the visible fraction equals the map's (measure it in a spec: sky fraction at cover 0.4 within +-0.1). Darken bases: attenuate sun and sky by the optical depth above the sample and drop the ground-bounce term to a physically small value. Upsample the half-resolution cloud buffer edge-aware (or march resolved near clouds at full resolution inside a tile as is done for small shells). Iterate against photographs at native 1440p in animated mode.

findings.defect: Interlaced scanlines. Blob-shaped areas of open sea are drawn with every other full-resolution pixel row brighter: x 460-640, y 570-650; x 250-600, y 640-720; x 650-760, y 590-620; x 980-1060, y 500-520. Column x = 540, rows 590-630, red channel: 105, 88, 106, 88, 108, 88 ... (about 5,200 pixels in the frame follow this pattern). The animated frame of the same view reads 78-80 there with no veil at all, only small dark shadow blobs; so the deterministic frame contains a phantom translucent veil, present in even rows and absent in odd rows, and it has lost the cloud shadow on the sea underneath. Deterministic mode is what every acceptance and mission screenshot uses. sampling.spec.ts does not see it: its region for this view is y 0.47-0.60 (rows 338-432), above the hatching.
findings.realReference: Open sea between cumulus seen from 5 km is a continuous surface with soft-edged cloud shadows; no row structure of any kind, and a still frame equals the temporally converged one.
findings.likelyCause: Inferred from the code, not traced at run time. Row parity at FULL resolution cannot come from the half-resolution buffers through a bilinear filter; the parity (upper row of each 2 x 2 block bright) fits the composite taking the FAR candidate for the upper pixel row of each block and the NEAR candidate for the lower one (compositeFsWgsl in src/render/atmosphere/shaders/march.ts: on a sea seen at a grazing angle dh.r != dh.g everywhere, and the 1 / (1 + diff * 200) weight makes each row take its own candidate). The two candidates disagree about the cloud: in marchFsWgsl 'behind' is computed from cloudGeom, and when the geometry texel is NO_CLOUD (3.0e38) while the colour texel still holds radiance, the far candidate adds Tc * cloud.rgb and the near candidate adds nothing (behind = 0). The altitude rule that would settle it only covers a camera above the shell top or below its bottom (h0 > cloudShell.w / h0 < cloudShell.z); a camera between 1.2 and 12.5 km, i.e. the whole ascent through the troposphere, falls through to the distance rule. Why the frozen frame has radiance without geometry there (and the accumulated one has neither) is not established; the resolve's 'o.color.a > 0.9995 || geom.b > 1.0e37 -> NO_CLOUD' branch keeps the colour while dropping the geometry.
findings.fixDirection: Make the two candidates agree by construction: when the nearest surface of the block lies below the cloud base (hNear < cloudShell.z) and the eye is above the cloud base, every cloud on the ray is in front of it (behind = 1) whatever the geometry texel says; and never let the resolve write colour with a < 1 next to NO_CLOUD geometry (zero the colour, or keep the last geometry). Then find why the frozen step phase produces the veil at all. Extend sampling.spec.ts: run the row-period-2 test on full-resolution rows over the whole frame below the horizon, in both modes, and compare frozen and accumulated frames there.

findings.defect: Whatever a cloud shades turns navy blue instead of grey. Under an overcast deck (clouds-under-deck.png) the deck is neutral grey (120, 117, 117) but the sea is (16, 25, 42), the island (54, 65, 87) and the haze over the far islands (89, 101, 125): a blue dusk under a white ceiling. At daylight exposure the ground under the deck is (2, 4, 10) (clouds-shadow-under-deck.png). From 10 km the cloud shadows on the island are indistinguishable from open sea: shadow on land at (673, 583) = (78, 98, 131), open ocean at (680, 673) = (80, 96, 125), so shadows read as lakes cut into the island (ascent-10km.png x 560-760, y 540-640). From the pad, cloud shadows on the mountains and on the plain are flat navy patches with crisp outlines, far darker than the lit ground beside them and a different hue (clouds-ground-cumulus.png y 440-540).
findings.realReference: Under an overcast the light is neutral: grey sea reflecting the cloud base, land in its own colours at 5-25 % of clear-sky illuminance, grey-white haze. In the shadow of a cumulus on a partly cloudy day the ground keeps its hue at roughly a quarter to a third of the sunlit brightness, because the clouds themselves are bright diffusers.
findings.likelyCause: Nothing published by the package knows about clouds except the direct-sun shadow. src/render/core/lighting/deferred.ts lines 229-260 light shaded terrain with 'atmosphere.skyIrradianceLut' (clear sky, blue) and reflect 'atmosphere.skyViewLut' (in-scatter only, no clouds) in water; in marchFsWgsl (shaders/march.ts line 234) only o.direct is multiplied by atmoCloudShadowOnRay while o.multi stays the clear-sky multiple scattering, so the air under a deck glows blue. The light that a cloud layer transmits and scatters downwards is not represented anywhere.
findings.fixDirection: Give the ambient a cloud term: from the coverage map and the shadow map derive, per point, a cloud cover above and its diffuse transmittance, and replace the clear-sky irradiance by mix(clear sky, white transmitted and side-scattered cloud light) (publish it as a second factor/texture or fold it into what setCloudShadowParams hands to the core: needs a request to core-support). Apply the same factor to o.multi below the cloud base in the march and the aerial volume, and add the cloud layer to the sky-view table (or publish a cloud-aware variant) so water under an overcast reflects grey. Assert in a spec that ground, sea and haze under a deck are neutral (|R - B| / luminance small) and that a cumulus shadow on terrain keeps 20-35 % of the lit luminance.

findings.defect: Clouds do not dim as the sun gets low. On the crescent Earth the brightest cloud pixel per column stays near white all the way across: 203 at the sunward limb (sun about 65 deg up), 193 where the sun is about 15 deg up, 167 where it is about 5 deg up, then falls to black within 12 px. The day side therefore ends in a hard edge of full-white cloud, and the clouds at the terminator carry orange-brown outlines (earth-moon-distance.png x 640-790, y 90-380) because only their thin edges are dim enough to show the reddened sun. The same thing makes the sunset cloudscape from the ground one uniform bright mustard instead of a range from lit to shaded.
findings.realReference: DSCOVR, Apollo 8 and Apollo 17 frames: cloud brightness follows the cosine of the solar zenith angle; towards the terminator the decks go grey, then pink, with long shadows, over several hundred kilometres. A cloud deck with the sun 5 deg up is roughly a tenth as bright as one at noon.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/atmosphere/shaders/clouds.ts, cloudMarchFsWgsl, the lighting of a sample (lines 698-726). 'highOrders = cloudLight.x * thick * (0.4 + 0.6 * saturate(muS)) / (PI * (1.0 + kd * tau * max(muS, 0.15)))': tau is the optical depth along the sun line, which grows as 1 / muS, so the denominator is constant and the term keeps 40 % of its noon value at muS = 0; nothing accounts for the foreshortening of the sunlight falling on a horizontally extended layer. For unresolved cloud the six cone samples span 'reach = max(sunReachM, 3 * footprint)' at mip-averaged density, and atmoCloudShadowAt clamps muS to 0.05 with a fixed farShadowOpticalDepth 2, so self-shadowing at a grazing sun is far too weak.
findings.fixDirection: For stratiform and unresolved (fraction) cloud make the returned radiance proportional to the flux on the layer, E * muS * R(tau, muS) / PI, with a two-stream or tabulated reflectance, instead of a per-sample term that does not fall with muS; for resolved shapes let the cone march carry the dimming (longer reach at low sun, no 0.15 floor). Add a spec: mean cloud luminance over an overcast patch at sun elevations 60, 30, 10 and 3 deg must follow muS within a stated band, and the crescent view must show a gradient across the terminator.

findings.defect: The near cloud-shadow map shows through the cloud lighting and the light shafts whenever the view looks towards the sun. (a) Sunset from the ground: a row of dark sawtooth triangles in the cloud band over the sun (clouds-ground-sunset.png x 420-760, y 350-410) and ruler-straight lit and shaded wedges on the ground (x 700-1280, y 465-545). (b) Sun 40 deg up, looking into it: the cloud in front of the sun is shaded in axis-aligned staircase facets with straight treads 15-30 px long (clouds-ground-cumulus-into-sun.png x 420-700, y 170-260), and the silver lining is a beaded 1-2 px outline. (c) From orbit at a 4 deg sun: a comb of parallel vertical lines 2-3 px apart in the air and on the cloud edge next to the deck (leo-low-sun.png x 440-560, y 620-720).
findings.realReference: Crepuscular rays and cloud self-shadowing are smooth: shafts with soft edges that widen with distance (the sun is half a degree wide: 9 m of penumbra per kilometre), silver linings that are a graded glow, lit ground patches at sunset with edges hundreds of metres soft.
findings.likelyCause: The shadow map (clouds.ts placeShadow; shaders/clouds.ts cloudShadowFsWgsl) is 1024^2 over 60 km (59 m texels), projected along the sun line with the elevation clamped to SHADOW_MIN_ELEVATION 4 deg, so one texel is stretched 14 times along the sun azimuth at sunset. atmoCloudShadowAt (shaders/march.ts line 38) reads it with one bilinear tap and combines three unlike channels after interpolation, clamp((g - s) * b, 0, r): a front distance interpolated across a cloud edge is a ramp, which gives teeth and facets. The cloud march adds it beyond the 2,500 m cone ('tau += -log(atmoCloudShadowAt(endPos ...))'), so texel blocks appear inside the cloud. In deterministic mode the shadow lookup in the air march has no dither (misc.z = 0), which freezes the comb.
findings.fixDirection: Resolve the three channels per texel and interpolate the resulting transmittance (four taps, or store a filterable representation such as exponential / moment optical depth); widen the filter with distance from the occluder (PCSS-style, sun angular radius); at low sun use a warped or cascaded map along the sun azimuth instead of a 4 deg clamp, or fall back to a short ray march through the density for shafts; dither the lookup with blue noise in the cloud march as well and keep a spatial dither in deterministic mode. Re-shoot sunset, into-sun and low-sun orbit close-ups at 1440p.

findings.defect: Cloud decks seen from above are covered in contour lines. With the shipped tunables from 25 km the whole overcast is a vermiculated pattern of nested wavy iso-lines, like wood grain or a topographic map (tunables-shipped.png, e.g. x 380-780, y 330-590). From 6 km straight down, the smooth part of the deck is drawn as flat terraces with outlines and meets the textured part along a hard boundary (shadow-lit-quad-above-the-deck.png x 60-430, y 280-450). At a shallow angle the deck is dunes with dark smudged pits and hairline creases (clouds-above-deck.png). In animated mode the lines turn into a sandpaper stipple (perf-above-a-deck-1440p.png, clouds-quality-0.7-above-deck.png). From 400 km an overcast is grey marble with bright veins along the noise cell edges (shadow-lit-quad-low-orbit.png).
findings.realReference: A stratocumulus deck from above: closed cells with bright centres and darker, thinner edges, lumpy cauliflower relief with soft continuous shading, no lines; from orbit a cellular texture, never bright veins on grey.
findings.likelyCause: shaders/clouds.ts march loop. Slabs are restarted at the cloud surface and each slab is lit once at its opacity-weighted depth; slabs that add under 4 % reuse the previous slab's light (reuseBelow). The number of slabs a ray spends in the bright skin changes in steps across the surface, and with the step phase frozen (xi = 0.5) each step is an iso-line; the source comment itself names 'contour bands, sand' as the failure of slab placement. The smooth/terraced versus textured boundary is the switch 'shaped = (low && den.resolved > 0.5) || den.relief > 1.0' (a threshold, not a blend). The veins are the Worley-cell channel (nb.a, meso.g) entering density and relief with creases.
findings.fixDirection: Remove the quantisation rather than dithering it: light every slab in the first few mean free paths (no reuse there), interpolate the lighting between consecutive lit slabs, and place slab boundaries by accumulated optical depth instead of by distance; blend the shaped and smooth representations over a range of den.resolved / relief instead of switching. Build the top relief from a smooth fBm plus cells with dark (thin) edges. Add a spec that looks for iso-line structure on an overcast from 6 and 25 km (gradient-direction coherence or Laplacian zero-crossing density) in both modes.

findings.defect: Far cloud seen edge-on is built from horizontal bars and 2 px blocks. The horizon bank at 10 km is ruled with horizontal lines 100-250 px long and contains a rectangular darker block with straight vertical ends (ascent-10km.png x 560-980, y 365-420; perf-ascent-10-km-1440p.png x 1100-1740, y 720-830). The far part of a deck just under the camera shows the same bars and 4 px blocks (clouds-deck-top.png x 0-320, y 340-400). From low orbit the cloud streets towards the limb are a knitted stair-step lattice of 2 x 2 px blocks (leo-day-limb.png x 0-420, y 400-560; leo-day.png x 0-330, y 220-340). The hand-off calls this residual 'faint'; in the deterministic acceptance frames it is plain at 1:1. (The perf-*.png frames were written a few minutes before the last source change of the package; all functional frames are current: suite re-run through the gate on 2026-11-11, 45 passed, 1 skipped.)
findings.realReference: A distant cloud bank is a soft continuous band with a hazy top; cloud streets near the limb from the ISS are fine continuous streaks that compress smoothly into the haze.
findings.likelyCause: Half-resolution buffer with one ray per 2 x 2 block: with the step phase frozen and, from orbit, the sub-pixel positions switched off (cloudJitter amplitude 0 beyond about 150 km), each of the four pixels of a block keeps the result of its own single ray; rows that graze a thin layer alternate between hit and miss. The march reads the cloud colour bilinearly but the geometry with a nearest textureLoad (march.ts line 186), so the air in front of a far bank is laid in per-texel blocks.
findings.fixDirection: For rays that cross a layer at a grazing angle integrate the layer analytically over the pixel's vertical footprint (the altitude range one pixel row covers at that distance), not only over the step; resolve the four pixels of a block with a spatial filter weighted by cloud depth when they disagree; interpolate cloud geometry with the same weights as the colour. Review ascent-10km and leo-day-limb at 1440p, deterministic and animated.

findings.defect: From 25 km upwards the clouds are a blurred overlay. (1) They are visibly softer than the surface under them: at 80 km the island's relief lines are crisp while every cloud is an out-of-focus blob (ascent-80km.png x 200-700, y 400-720). (2) Broken fields are equal-sized popcorn, the cell structure of the noise (leo-day.png x 640-1000, y 420-600). (3) Large clouds are flat with posterised two-tone patches and straight-sided brighter plateaus (leo-day.png x 660-960, y 560-720; ascent-25km.png x 640-830, y 440-500). (4) No cloud casts a visible shadow on the sea from 400 km, although the brief asks for decks casting shadows. (5) From 60,000 km and the Moon's distance every system is one flat white with blurred outlines; the baked coverage map (data/tiles/earth/globals/cloudCoverage.png) holds streaks and cells that the render does not show.
findings.realReference: ISS and airliner photographs: clouds are the sharpest thing in the frame, with texture at every scale, bright tops and grey flanks, and a dark shadow displaced down-sun from every cloud; whole-disc images show graded opacity, from thin veils through textured decks to bright convective cores.
findings.likelyCause: Half-resolution cloud buffer at one ray per 2 x 2 block, noise one mip above the footprint, and 'cloudNoiseKeep' replacing the noise by its mean past mip 4-5.5; the coverage map is read at 'max(log2(footprint / texel), 1.0)', never at its finest level. Opacity saturates: lowCoverageGain 0.9 on a map of which a quarter is at 0.9-1, so col.cLow is 1 over whole systems and the extinction variation (lowDensityVariation) fades out with mesoKeep / largeKeep. Shadows from orbit: the near map is 1,920 km wide at 400 km altitude (1.9 km texels) and band-limited further by shadowFilter; the far term is a constant optical depth 2 times the mip-filtered coverage.
findings.fixDirection: March clouds at full resolution wherever they are unresolved fractions (cheap: few steps), or upsample with depth and coverage awareness; read the coverage map at its finest level from orbit and use its value as optical thickness (graded white), not only as cover; keep mesoscale opacity variation at every distance by baking it into a mip-consistent texture. For shadows from orbit add a ground-projected term from the coverage map offset by cloud-top height along the sun line, at the pixel's footprint. Bake more dynamic range into cloudCoverage (request to bake-earth: the map clips at 1).

findings.defect: Pepper holes in the full-resolution tile march. Inside and at the edge of white cloud there are isolated single pixels of saturated navy or black, darker than the open ocean next to them: earth-60000km.png at (700, 225), (714, 232), (681, 236), (582, 241) and about 50 more (e.g. 198 -> 104 -> 196 along one row); earth-60000km-crescent.png 17; black dots in the cloud near the terminator in small-shell-clouds-fov10.5.png; two blue dots in the 45 px Earth of earth-moon-distance-wide.png. The 1440p frames of the same view (disc over 512 px, half-resolution path) have none. Cloud outlines in the tile path are also binary and stair-stepped. With any camera motion these pixels will twinkle.
findings.realReference: A planet disc a few hundred pixels across has anti-aliased, partially covered cloud edges and no isolated dark pixels.
findings.likelyCause: cloudMarchFsWgsl(fine = true) in shaders/clouds.ts: one ray through the pixel centre, xi = 0.5, no temporal accumulation. A pixel darker than the sea is shaded sea seen through a one-pixel hole: the deferred far shadow (coverage map) says cloud, the march returned none. Candidates: the early out for columns 'above every cloud top the map allows' (cloudColumnAt with hLow) combined with long coarsened steps (budget shared between spans, 'steps < budget + 12'), or the sliver path leaving wSum <= 1e-5.
findings.fixDirection: Reproduce at the listed pixels (viewFromSpace(66371000, 30, 25), 1280 x 720) and log steps, spans and wSum; guarantee at least one integrated sample per layer per ray in the fraction regime. Anti-alias the tile march: 4 sub-samples per pixel are affordable at 512 x 512, or accumulate jittered rays. Extend smallshell.spec.ts with an isolated-dark-pixel count inside cloud (expect 0).

findings.defect: The cloud history does not follow a change of lighting, and the screen border shows it. In clouds-ground-after-sunset.png (corner x 0-160, y 0-100) the outermost pixel row at the top and the outermost columns left and right are dark navy (45, 40, 60) while the cloud one pixel further in is sunset brown (125, 100, 75): mean difference 42 levels along the top edge, 31 left, 26 right. Reading of the resolve code: the border pixels never use history (uvPrev must be more than a texel inside) and show what the clouds look like now, 1.5 deg after sunset; the interior still carries the light of the previous scene (sun 3 deg up) 40 frames later. So this acceptance image does not show the after-sunset state, and any view has a 1-2 px frame whenever the lighting moves. clouds-deck-top.png has a 2 px strip of different brightness on the left edge at x 0-2, y 338-378.
findings.realReference: Cloud brightness follows the sun without lag and uniformly to the edge of the frame.
findings.likelyCause: CLOUD_RESOLVE_FS_WGSL in shaders/clouds.ts: a still pixel blends its own march with weight misc.w = 0.125 once every four frames (time constant about 30 frames) and the neighbourhood clamp is scaled by motion ('not at all to a pixel that has not moved'), so nothing rejects history when the sun, an eclipse or the exposure-normalised radiance changes; the history is also re-scaled by the exposure ratio, which amplifies the stale light as the metering opens up. clouds.ts line 662 only invalidates history on a missed frame or a target change.
findings.fixDirection: Always apply a (wider) neighbourhood clamp, or detect lighting change (sun direction relative to the body, sun visibility, large change of mean fresh radiance) and raise the blend weight or reset; store history normalised by the sun illuminance at the sample so that a change of sun colour and intensity re-lights it at once. Treat border pixels like the rest (clamp uvPrev instead of rejecting). Spec: step the sun by 5 deg with a static camera and require convergence within 8 frames and no border difference.

findings.defect: Stair-stepped limb. The lower edge of the night-side limb glow, with its thin orange line, is a staircase of 2 px steps with dark notches (leo-night-limb.png x 280-720, y 375-400); at the terminator the boundary between the lit limb and the dark planet is stepped in 3-4 px blocks and the glow is ruled with faint horizontal lines (leo-terminator.png x 620-960, y 290-330). On a moving limb this crawls.
findings.realReference: Orbital sunrise from the ISS: a smooth arc, red at the bottom through yellow-white to blue, with a clean lower edge.
findings.likelyCause: Half-resolution march composited across the planet silhouette where the cloud buffer changes the far/near candidates (march.ts composite: nearest-depth fallback picks whole half-resolution texels), plus cloud geometry read with a nearest textureLoad. The first review saw it only with clouds on.
findings.fixDirection: Use the full-resolution tile march for a band of pixels around the limb at any distance (the rectangle of the silhouette is known from select.ts), or interpolate the candidates along the silhouette with the full-resolution depth; add a limb-edge smoothness check to sky.spec.ts with clouds on.

findings.defect: Twilight skies are grey-lavender. Top of frame at sunset (92, 99, 122), ten minutes before (59, 69, 87) with a neutral grey zone (98, 97, 105) above the glow, and (108, 109, 142) over the anti-twilight arch: red equals green, so the sky is purple-grey where the brief asks for a dark blue zenith. The Belt of Venus and the Earth-shadow band themselves are present and good.
findings.realReference: At sunset the sky 30-40 deg up is still clearly blue (green well above red), deepening to indigo at the zenith after sunset because of ozone absorption; the transition above the glow is pale yellow into pale blue, not neutral grey.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/render/earth.atmosphere.json: ozoneAbsorption red 1.9e-6, a stated compromise between 0.65e-6 and the band average 2.7e-6 (hand-off section 6); three sRGB-primary coefficients cannot follow the spectral reddening of twilight paths.
findings.fixDirection: Integrate the tables over more bands (for example 6-8 wavelengths in the transmittance and multi-scattering tables, converted to sRGB at the end), or fit the ozone and Rayleigh coefficients per channel against a spectral reference for sun elevations +5 to -6 deg and assert G/R of the sky 40 deg up, not only R < G < B.

findings.defect: Inside cloud the frame is a flat, dark, slightly brown grey: (76, 73, 70) at daylight exposure, with no brightening towards the sun or the top and no wisps passing the camera.
findings.realReference: Flying through cloud is a bright white-out, lighter overhead, with visible streaming fog texture near the window and a glow in the direction of the sun when the top is near.
findings.likelyCause: Step minimum 60 m and no near-field detail (finest erosion octave only within 40 m of footprint and only at the surface); the sample's light inside deep cloud is the reused last slab; ambient 'sky / (1 + kd * above)' collapses with the very large optical depth of the 0.9 cover column (lowExtinction 0.06 over 1,900 m plus the deep fill).
findings.fixDirection: Add a near-camera fog term with small-scale animated density variation inside cloud, and a directional in-cloud glow (forward-scattered sun through the remaining optical depth); check the luminance against a diffusion estimate for the depth below the top.

findings.defect: Hard boundaries between cloud regimes. With stepFactor 0.05 / stepMinM 200 / stepMaxM 3000 (inside the accepted ranges) the deck ends at a sharp circular arc across the frame (y about 300-350) beyond which the cloud is a translucent blue sheet; the spec passes on its numbers. With shipped values a straight diagonal line crosses the deck from (0, 690) to (400, 535) in leo-low-sun.png: saturated featureless white on one side, stippled cream on the other.
findings.realReference: A deck keeps one appearance out to the horizon; no straight or circular lines.
findings.likelyCause: tunables-coarse-steps: rays run out of step budget ('steps < budget + 12', coarsen) and return what they have, so the far field loses its opacity at a fixed distance; the same mechanism is reachable with shipped values when qualityScale lowers the budget (cloudSteps x q^2). leo-low-sun: cause not established; the line runs along the east-west direction (it heads for the vanishing point), which points at something keyed to latitude or to a regime threshold (deep column / sheet relief switch) rather than to distance.
findings.fixDirection: When the budget is short lengthen the remaining steps so the ray always reaches the end of its spans (opacity must not depend on the budget); assert in tunables.spec.ts that mean transmittance per screen band is uniform. Find the leo-low-sun line with a per-pixel debug output of the regime (shaped / sheet / deep column) added to the lab.

findings.defect: Outside this package, for the lead: the sun above the limb is a flat grey gaussian disc about 200 px in radius with a soft edge around a white core. It reads as a halo sprite, which PROMPT.txt rules out.
findings.realReference: The sun from orbit photographed at daylight exposure: a small clipped disc with diffraction spikes or a tight veiling glare that falls off steeply; no uniform grey ball.
findings.likelyCause: Render core bloom / sun-disc glare (src/render/core/post), not src/render/atmosphere: there is no air between the eye and the sun in this view.
findings.fixDirection: Hand to the owner of the post chain: energy-conserving bloom with a steep kernel, or a lens model with a physically shaped glare.
